annotation.title_clean: Automation hits the knowledge worker: ChatGPT and the future of work
annotation.title_en: Automation hits the knowledge worker: ChatGPT and the future of work
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Berg, J.; Gmyrek, P. (International Labour Office)
annotation.venue: ILO Voices - The Future of Work Podcast (ILO Research Department policy brief)
annotation.summary_en: ILO policy brief on how LLMs like ChatGPT affect knowledge workers. It argues task transformation is likelier than mass job loss, stresses job quality alongside quantity, and highlights precarious data-labelling work and the digital divide. It recommends social dialogue and occupational safety regulation for new AI-related occupations.
key_provisions_or_claims: 644-997 million jobs (19.6-30.4% of global employment) are knowledge work
LLMs more likely to transform tasks than eliminate jobs
Job quality matters as much as job quantity
Data-labelling 'invisible workers' face low pay, precarity and psychosocial risks needing OSH regulation
Social dialogue should be used from the design stage of the technology
